subject: Security/compliance follow-up: subprocessor list & SOC 2 status
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Snyder <john.snyder@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: security & subprocessor follow-up

Hi John / Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great to hear more about Acme's plans for embedded AI in customer support. As promised, quick recap of the security/compliance items we committed to follow up on: 

- SOC 2 status: we provided a high-level SOC 2 summary during the call. John asked for the latest report or an attestation.
- Subprocessor list: you asked for a full list of subprocessors (cloud providers, analytics, monitoring, deps).
- Data boundaries & HIPAA/GDPR: clarification on how we segment customer data and options for data residency (VPC/private deployment).
- Vendor security questionnaire: you mentioned starting an initial vendor security questionnaire (Excel).

Next steps (for Acme):
1) If you can share the vendor questionnaire, we can start filling it out.
2) We'll attach the current subprocessor spreadsheet and SOC 2 high-level summary in the follow-up email.
3) Recommend a 30-min sync next week if you want to walk the subprocessor mapping and data flows.

I've looped in Aditya from our security/product team for any technical follow-ups.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: deck-demo-acme.pdf (presentation)]

From: John Snyder <john.snyder@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: security & subprocessor follow-up

Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — this is helpful. A couple quick asks from our side as we triage this with procurement/security: 

1) Can you attach the full subprocessor list (including cloud infra providers, monitoring, logging, and any third-party APIs used at inference/runtime)? We need vendor names, what data they see, and if they have access to customer plaintext.
2) SOC 2: do you have a Type II report or a formal attestation we can share with our InfoSec team? If not, a timeline for Type II would be good.
3) GDPR/HIPAA: any standard customer controls for data retention, deletion, and encryption at rest/in transit?

I'm attaching our vendor security questionnaire (initial version). Could you get that filled and returned? We can then feed up to procurement.

Thanks —
John
John Snyder
Head of Procurement | Acme Corp
john.snyder@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0987

[Attachment: Acme_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Snyder <john.snyder@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: security & subprocessor follow-up

John —

Appreciate the clear asks. We're attaching the materials you requested and proposing the following timeline: 

Attachments included in this email:
- redwood_subprocessors_2026-03.xlsx (full subprocessor mapping; columns: vendor, service type, region, data access scope)
- SOC2-summary-2025Q4.pdf (executive summary + scope; full Type II report available under NDA)
- vendor-questionnaire-acme.xlsx (pre-filled answers for the first pass)

Quick answers inline: 
- Subprocessors & access: the spreadsheet includes cloud infra (AWS/GCP), monitoring (Datadog), observability/logging (S3/Cloud Storage with restricted access), and a small set of managed services used for telemetry. For each vendor we call out whether they can access plaintext customer data or only aggregated/hashed telemetry.
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II for our control environment in 2025 (coverage through Q4 2025). We can share the full report under a standard NDA or via secure share with your InfoSec team.
- GDPR/HIPAA controls: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), data residency via our private deployment options, and per-customer retention policies. The questionnaire has references to the controls and a few links to our security docs.

Suggested next steps: 
1) Confirm whether your InfoSec prefers the full SOC 2 under NDA or a direct secure share.
2) Review the attached pre-filled questionnaire and flag any follow-ups. We can have Aditya join a 30-min session to walk the subprocessor spreadsheet and answer any technical questions.
3) If desired, we can open a support ticket to provision a temporary secure share point for the full report.

Proposed times for a short sync: Tue 3/24 10:00–10:30am PT or Wed 3/25 2:00–2:30pm PT. Which works best?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

[Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2026-03.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet); SOC2-summary-2025Q4.pdf (PDF); vendor-questionnaire-acme.xlsx (Excel - pre-filled)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, John Snyder <john.snyder@acme.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: security & subprocessor follow-up

Hi all — looping in with a few clarifications from our security team. Thanks for the questionnaire, John. A few notes: 

- Full subprocessor visibility: the attached spreadsheet (from Marissa) is the canonical list. For each vendor we indicate data access scope; we do not share plaintext customer data with external analytics vendors unless explicitly authorized by the customer.
- SOC 2 Type II: Redwood's most recent Type II report covers the period Jan–Dec 2025. We typically provide the full report under NDA; a redacted attestation can be shared without NDA. If Acme wants the full report, we'll start the secure share/NDA flow.
- Timeline for outstanding items: we can return the completed vendor questionnaire with clarifying notes within 3 business days after you confirm any targeted questions. If you need technical evidence (configurations, KMS proofs), that may take 5–7 business days.
- Data residency/HIPAA: we offer Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment for PHI workloads and have controls for encryption at rest/in transit. If Acme is pursuing HIPAA, we recommend a short technical review to map the PHI flow.

Marissa — happy to join the sync on Tue 3/24 10:00 PT. John/Sarah — please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
